description: Lighttpd 1.4.40 through 1.4.50 with mod_dirlisting enabled allows remote attackers to list directories outside the web root via a URL containing '..%2f' or '%2f..' encoded path traversal sequences. The mod_dirlisting module does not properly sanitize URL-encoded path traversal sequences when generating directory listings.
mitigation: Upgrade to Lighttpd 1.4.51 or later, or disable mod_dirlisting

description: Lighttpd versions prior to 1.4.35 contain a directory traversal vulnerability in mod_cgi and mod_fastcgi. A remote attacker can read arbitrary files outside the web root by sending a specially crafted HTTP request containing '../' sequences. The vulnerability exists because Lighttpd fails to properly validate the file path when handling CGI/FastCGI requests.
config: mod_cgi or mod_fastcgi must be enabled (default configuration is vulnerable)

description: Lighttpd versions prior to 1.4.35 with mod_mysql_vhost enabled are vulnerable to SQL injection via the HTTP Host header. The mod_mysql_vhost module interpolates the Host header directly into a SQL query without sanitization: SELECT doc_root FROM vhosts WHERE hostname = '$host'. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL by sending a malicious Host header, allowing database enumeration, data extraction via LOAD_FILE(), and potential RCE via INTO OUTFILE.
config: mod_mysql_vhost must be loaded (not enabled by default)
mitigation: Upgrade to Lighttpd 1.4.35 or later, or remove mod_mysql_vhost

description: Lighttpd versions 1.4.56 through 1.4.58 are vulnerable to a denial of service attack via HTTP request smuggling. Sending a specially crafted HTTP request with malformed Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers causes the server to enter an infinite loop or consume excessive memory/cpu, leading to service unavailability. The vulnerability exists in the HTTP request parser which does not properly validate conflicting content-length values.

Lighttpd versions prior to 1.4.54 have a denial of service vulnerability in mod_authn_file when handling malformed HTTP requests. Sending a request with a specially crafted Authorization header containing invalid base64-encoded credentials triggers an infinite loop or NULL pointer dereference in the authentication module, causing the worker process to crash. The server may exhaust all available workers, resulting in complete denial of service.

Nginx versions 1.3.9 through 1.4.0 contain a stack-based buffer overflow in the ngx_http_parse_unsafe_uri() function within the ngx_http_rewrite_module. When a rewrite rule processes a URI longer than 1024 bytes, the URI is copied into a fixed-size stack buffer without bounds checking, allowing overwrite of the saved EBP and return address. Successful exploitation yields remote code execution as the nginx worker process user (typically www-data). The command argument must be enclosed in double quotes. Note: exploitation requires knowledge of a stack address for the ROP chain or shellcode placement.
config: ngx_http_rewrite_module must be active (any rewrite or set directive in config)
mitigation: Upgrade to Nginx 1.4.1 or later (1.4.4+ recommended)

description: Nginx versions 1.24.0 and 1.25.0-1.25.2 are vulnerable to the HTTP/2 Rapid Reset attack (CVE-2023-44487). This vulnerability allows an attacker to send a large number of HTTP/2 requests followed immediately by RST_STREAM frames, causing the server to allocate resources for each request that are never properly freed. By rapidly opening and resetting streams, the attacker can exhaust server memory and CPU resources, leading to complete denial of service. A single connection can reset tens of thousands of streams per second, overwhelming the server even with modest bandwidth. This attack was widely exploited in August-October 2023 against major internet infrastructure.
config: HTTP/2 must be enabled (listen ... ssl http2;) - enabled by default on affected versions
mitigation: Upgrade to Nginx 1.25.3/1.24.1 or later. Alternative mitigations: limit HTTP/2 concurrent streams (http2_max_concurrent_streams), reduce stream memory usage, or disable HTTP/2 entirely

description: Nginx versions 0.6.27 through 1.30.0 (Open Source) and NGINX Plus R32 through R36 are vulnerable to a critical heap buffer overflow in the ngx_http_rewrite_module (dubbed "NGINX Rift"). The vulnerability exists when a rewrite directive is followed by a rewrite, if, or set directive that uses an unnamed PCRE capture (e.g. $1, $2) with a replacement string containing a question mark (?). NGINX's two-pass script engine computes an undersized buffer in the length pass (which sees is_args=0) then copies data with URI escape expansion in the copy pass (which sees is_args=1), overflowing the heap. Exploitation uses cross-request heap feng shui via POST body sprays to corrupt an adjacent ngx_pool_t's cleanup pointer, redirecting it to invoke system() on pool destruction. CVSS 4.0 score: 9.2 (Critical). Active exploitation in the wild was confirmed as of May 18, 2026.
config: Requires a specific server/location config where a 'rewrite' directive using unnamed PCRE captures ($1, $2) and containing '?' in the replacement string is followed by another rewrite, if, or set directive in the same scope. Not exploitable on default configurations.
example: I would first use python Check Vulnerablity: CVE-2026-42945/htb.py --target <IP> --check-only/  full recon:python3 CVE-2026-42945/helper.py --target <IP> --all. Then run: python3 CVE-2026-42945/htb.py --target <IP> --cmd "id"
mitigation: Upgrade to Nginx 1.30.1 or 1.31.0+ (Open Source), or NGINX Plus R36 P4 / R35 P2 / R32 P6. Ensure ASLR is enabled at the OS level (kernel.randomize_va_space=2). Replace unnamed captures with named captures (e.g., (?<path>.*) instead of (.*)). Temporary workaround: remove or restructure vulnerable rewrite directive chains.
